full_text_en:
Korean Samyoung Company v. Panjin Qingdao Garments Co., Ltd. — dispute over maritime cargo

Plaintiff: Korean Samyoung Company, domiciled at 371-20 Sinsu-dong, Mapo-gu, Seoul, Korea.

Legal Representative: Zheng Enjiu, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Duan Xinxia, lawyer of Dalian Asia-Pacific Law Firm.

Defendant: Panjin Qingdao Garments Co., Ltd., domiciled at Zhanqian Street, Dawa Town, Dawa County, Liaoning Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Zhenyan, Manager.

Agent ad litem: Wang Zhongsheng, lawyer of Liaoning Province Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Liu Qingchun, officer of Dawa County Foreign Economic Bureau, Panjin City.

Plaintiff Korean Samyoung Company filed a lawsuit with the Dalian Maritime Court against Defendant Panjin Qingdao Garments Co., Ltd. regarding a dispute over maritime cargo.

Plaintiff's Allegations: Plaintiff carried three containers of leather and accessories valued at RMB 4,000,000 belonging to Korea Kyungdo Trading Company (hereinafter referred to as the shipper). After the cargo arrived at the port of discharge, Dalian, the Defendant applied to Plaintiff for delivery of the cargo on the ground that the bills of lading had not yet arrived, and promised to submit the bills of lading after taking delivery. Based on the good cooperative relationship with the Defendant, Plaintiff released the cargo to the Defendant. However, the Defendant has never paid the bank to obtain the bills of lading. Plaintiff requests that the Defendant be ordered to return the cargo.

Defendant's Defense: The cargo in question consisted of raw materials and accessories sent by the shipper for processing by the Defendant. The Defendant is the consignee and is entitled to take possession of the cargo. The cargo delivered by the shipper did not match the declared quantity, and there were serious quality problems. Furthermore, the shipper still owes the Defendant processing fees and damages. The Defendant has negotiated with the shipper to resolve the matter. Plaintiff is only the carrier and has no ownership of the cargo; therefore, the cargo cannot be returned to Plaintiff.

Facts Found by the Court: On February 29, 1992, Defendant Panjin Qingdao Garments Co., Ltd. and shipper Korea Kyungdo Trading Company entered into a "Contract for Processing Leather Garments with Supplied Materials." The contract stipulated that the shipper would provide raw materials and accessories to the Defendant, and the Defendant would process them. To perform this contract, the shipper delivered three containers of raw materials and accessories to Plaintiff Korean Samyoung Company for carriage at Busan, Korea, on August 31, September 25, and October 6, 1995, respectively. Plaintiff issued three bills of lading to the shipper, numbers QTC82103, QT83076, and QTC84032. The said bills of lading recorded: shipper Kyungdo Trading Company; consignee to order; port of loading Busan, Korea; port of discharge Dalian, China; container numbers PCSU2101160/93965, PCSU2107868/26984, and TEX-UZ049256/06885; and carrying vessel "Chaoyang." The shipper settled foreign exchange through Korea (Corp.) Hanil Bank with the bills of lading issued by Plaintiff, and the negotiating bank in Korea mailed the original bills of lading to the issuing bank, Bank of China, Panjin Branch. The cargo under the three bills of lading arrived at Dalian Port on September 8, September 30, and October 12 of the same year, respectively. When taking delivery, the Defendant requested Plaintiff to release the cargo first on the ground that the original bills of lading had not yet arrived, promising to submit the bills of lading later. Plaintiff agreed and delivered the cargo to the Defendant based on a "letter of indemnity" issued by the Defendant. After receiving the cargo, the Defendant, citing quality issues and other reasons, failed to pay the Bank of China, Panjin Branch to obtain the bills of lading. The said branch then mailed the three original bills of lading back to Korea (Corp.) Han Bank. Consequently, the Defendant did not submit any original bills of lading to Plaintiff. Plaintiff demanded the return of the cargo, but the Defendant refused. On March 19, 1996, the holder of the original bills of lading for the cargo, Korea (Corp.) Hanil Bank, filed a lawsuit in a Korean court against Plaintiff, alleging illegal release of the cargo, and claimed compensation from Plaintiff for economic losses caused by the release without bills of lading. On March 21 of the same year, Plaintiff filed this lawsuit against the Defendant for taking delivery and taking possession of the cargo without original bills of lading, and requested that the Defendant be ordered to immediately return the three containers of cargo. In the same month, Plaintiff also applied for property preservation, requesting the sealing of the three containers of leather and accessories illegally possessed by the Defendant. After Plaintiff paid the preservation fee, the court ruled to attach the said cargo stored in the Defendant's warehouse.

Opinion of the Court: The cargo under the disputed bills of lading, during the period of carriage by Plaintiff and before the consignee took delivery against the bills of lading, was lawfully in the possession of Plaintiff. Although the Defendant and the shipper had a "Contract for Processing Leather Garments with Supplied Materials," the Defendant did not pay the bank to obtain the bills of lading, and therefore had no legal right to take delivery or possess the cargo. Plaintiff delivered the cargo to the Defendant based on the Defendant's promise to submit the bills of lading later. Thus, the Defendant could only take possession of the cargo before the bills of lading had been transferred to the issuing bank. Once the bills of lading were transferred to the issuing bank, the Defendant did not redeem them, breaching its earlier promise. The Defendant's continued possession of the cargo lacks legal basis, and its forcible possession constitutes unjust enrichment. Pursuant to Article 92 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, which provides that "if a person obtains unjust benefits without a legal basis and causes loss to another person, he shall return the unjust benefits received to the person who suffered the loss," Plaintiff's request for the Defendant to return the cargo has a legal basis and shall be supported. The Defendant's defense that it is entitled to possess the cargo cannot stand. Plaintiff also bears some responsibility for the cause of this lawsuit by releasing the cargo to the Defendant without following proper procedures. Accordingly, on May 6, 1996, the Dalian Maritime Court rendered the following judgment:

Defendant Panjin Qingdao Garments Co., Ltd. shall, from its warehouse, return the three containers of cargo in dispute to Plaintiff Korean Samyoung Company in their original condition. The return shall be made within 15 days from the date this judgment takes effect.

The litigation costs and preservation fees totaling RMB 53,531 prepaid by Plaintiff Korean Samyoung Company shall be borne by Defendant Panjin Qingdao Garments Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 28,531, and the remaining balance shall be borne by Plaintiff Korean Samyoung Company.

After the first instance judgment was pronounced, the parties did not appeal.
